propositions: Step registry membership depends on a single import chain that can be silently broken by a routine 'remove unused import' cleanup, and this hazard is invisible to the schema, linter, and existing test_contracts.py
plan_review/workflow_ops.py (794 LOC) and llm/config.py (793 LOC) lack headroom guards while gate_dispatch_seam and structured_run_seam tests pin four and one paths respectively

test_gate_dispatch_seam.py asserts gate_dispatch.py < 700 with a justification about finalize_verdict call sites that no longer exist in that file (moved to plan_review_recovery.py and plan_review/workflow_ops.py)

Process-global STEP_REGISTRY is populated as an import side effect and cached in sys.modules, making in-process assertions unable to detect missing registrations when test ordering or prior imports have already populated it
Every 'uses:' field in gates/plan-review.yaml must resolve to STEP_REGISTRY at first-import time, not after test setup has populated it
Headroom assertions must run in subprocess isolation with clean sys.modules to observe first-import behavior, the only form that can catch a missed registration import
